newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus welcomes Russia-NATO partnership pact.
newsitem.headline: Belarus welcomes Russia-NATO partnership pact.

text.p: A minister from Belarus, which shares neighbouring Russia's opposition to plans by NATO to expand eastwards, welcomed Wednesday's deal on forming a new friendship between Moscow and the Western defence alliance.
"This will undoubtedly have a positive effect on the stabilisation of the situation in Europe and in the whole world," Deputy Foreign Minister Nina Mazay told Reuters.

She was speaking after Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana reached a deal intended to placate Russia before the alliance invites new members in eastern Europe to join.
Mazay said Belarus, a country of 10 million on Russia's western border which is forging closer ties with Moscow, would be helped in its own negotiations with NATO by the deal.
"But an agreement with Russia will create a favourable background for our interests," Mazay said.
President Alexander Lukashenko once referred to the Western defence alliance as a "monster" and he has consistently backed Moscow in its opposition to NATO expansion.
Lukashenko has urged NATO to conclude a separate treaty with his country and said a new "European order" should be established without the United States.
Belarus, like Russia, is a member of NATO's Partnership for Peace (PFP) programme but has not taken part in joint military manoeuvres or in officer exchanges with the alliance.
